newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads - Underperfrom N.America.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads - Underperfrom N.America.

text.p: Australian bonds underperformed against the U.S., and even more so against Canada, which rallied strongly on Friday as worries over a tightening by the Federal Reserve later this month continued to wane.

Debt markets were under pressure in early Asian trading on Monday as the U.S. dollar dropped sharply amid panic selling by Japanese investors, taking the gloss off Friday's advance in U.S. Treasuries.

The local market faces the 1997/98 Federal budget late on Tuesday, an event that is expected to produce a positive reaction, although it may still lag the U.S. market, which could see subdued outcomes to this week's inflation and retail sales data and further erode concerns of tighter monetary policy.
Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale Australia, expected the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread to trade in a 95-110 basis point range in the near-term.

"(U.S.) Inflation data released this week is expected to be benign, and following Greenspan's comments last week, the market is expected to lower the probability attached to a May 20 FOMC tightening," he added.

Comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Friday were taken by some analysts as hinting that the Fed will not tighten on May 20, although others felt there was no clear signal either way.

Meanwhile, domestic bonds outperformed New Zealand as short end yields rose after the RBNZ said that monetary conditions appeared to be settling at levels somewhat too low to be consistent with the intended stance of policy.
